runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical evidence-quality score based on current Environment Agency/DEFRA/GLA sources, explicit present-day versus climate-change scenario separation, and prevention of area-level flood mapping being treated as property- or parcel-specific risk without FRA and exact geometry.

sources.label: EA Flood risk assessments: applying for planning permission
sources.fact: Updated 28 May 2026; FRA may be required in Zones 2/3, Zone 1 sites of 1 hectare or more, plus-climate-change areas, surface-water risk areas and other specified cases; unsatisfactory or missing FRA can affect an application.

sources.label: EA National flood risk standing advice for LPAs
sources.fact: Updated 28 May 2026; LPAs should research the site, development class, FRA/SuDS requirements, tests and consultation triggers.

sources.label: EA Flood Zones 1, 2, 3 and 3b FRA guidance
sources.fact: Updated 28 May 2026; applicants must distinguish flood-zone and vulnerability/test requirements rather than infer risk from a single map label.

sources.label: EA Preparing a flood risk assessment: standing advice
sources.fact: Updated 28 May 2026; sets standing-advice routes and links sequential/exception tests and submission requirements.

sources.label: EA Flood risk assessments: climate change allowances
sources.fact: Climate-change allowances cover river flow, rainfall intensity, sea-level rise and other factors; development lifetime and scenario determine the allowance used.

sources.label: Flood Map for Planning - Flood Zones
sources.fact: Current Flood Zones dataset distinguishes Zones 2 and 3 based on annual probabilities while ignoring benefits of defences; Zone 1 is land outside Zones 2/3 and is not shown in the dataset.

sources.label: Surface Water Spatial Planning Extents - Present Day
sources.fact: Published 28 May 2026 generation; shows 0.1%, 1% and 3.3% annual exceedance probability extents and explicitly is not suitable for deciding whether an individual property is at risk.

sources.label: Surface Water Spatial Planning Depths - Present Day
sources.fact: Shows present-day surface-water depth bands for 0.1%, 1% and 3.3% AEP scenarios; intended as area-level planning information, not individual-property truth.

sources.label: Surface Water Spatial Planning Extents - Climate Change
sources.fact: Climate-change surface-water extents provide future scenarios and must not be mixed with present-day extents.

sources.label: Surface Water Spatial Planning Depths - Climate Change
sources.fact: Climate-change depth layers use AEP scenarios and depth bands; scenario/version must be retained in any parcel-level assessment.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Chapter 9 Sustainable Infrastructure
sources.fact: Adopted London Plan includes Policy SI12 Flood risk management and SI13 Sustainable drainage; policy context does not replace site-specific FRA or drainage design.

sources.label: London Sustainable Drainage Action Plan
sources.fact: The 2017-2022 action plan is historical strategic direction; current London work is moving through the surface-water strategy and SuDS delivery programmes, so historical action-plan dates must not be treated as a current site approval.

examples.result: LBBD49/XJ remains current; flood/SuDS policy cannot establish exact flood depth or drainage capacity without site geometry and FRA.
LBBD72/ZZ remains current; present-day and climate-change surface-water scenarios are kept separate.
LBBD64/XE remains not-permissioned; flood context cannot override planning status.
LBBD91/DI remains current; exact parcel relation and site-specific drainage/FRA evidence remain required.
Flood Zone mapping ignores defence benefits for zone classification; this is not converted into an annual-loss probability for a parcel.
Surface-water datasets explicitly are not individual-property risk determinations; no parcel promotion from map presence alone.
Climate-change allowances are tied to lifetime/scenario; present-day and future scenario evidence is not mixed.
London Plan SI12/SI13 are policy gates, not hydraulic-model results or sewer-capacity confirmation.
